messages.content: Hi there! It's lovely to chat with you today. How have you been doing generally lately? Anything been bringing you joy or keeping you busy?
It's been tough, to be honest. Work has been a grind lately. I've just been going through the motions, trying to keep my head above water. Nothing really exciting happening.

That sounds really draining – work being a grind and just going through the motions. It’s completely understandable to feel weighed down by that. On a related note, how has your energy level been feeling these days with everything going on at work?
It's been low. I wake up in the morning and just feel... heavy. Like I'm carrying a bag of bricks on my shoulders. I just want to lie back down.

That sounds incredibly difficult – waking up feeling heavy like that. It takes a lot of strength to even get out of bed when you feel that way. Thinking about how things have been generally, have you found yourself feeling more pessimistic about things lately, or less hopeful about the future?
Pessimistic. Definitely. I look at my bank account and I think, 'How am I going to pay the bills next month?' And I just don't see a way out. It feels like I'm drowning in debt.

That sounds incredibly stressful, worrying about bills and feeling like you’re drowning in debt. It’s completely understandable to feel pessimistic when facing those kinds of pressures. Beyond the financial worries, have you noticed if you’ve been feeling particularly sad or down lately, separate from the stress about work and money?

Yeah. It’s hard to separate the two, but I think I’m just... empty, you know? I used to have hobbies and stuff, but I just don't have the energy to pick up the guitar or watch a movie. It feels like I've just been running on fumes for months.

It sounds like that emptiness is really impacting what you used to enjoy, and that’s really tough. You mentioned having low energy and just running on fumes – I’m wondering, has that been making it hard to concentrate or focus on things, even simple tasks? And along with that, have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite recently?

Yeah, everything is a struggle. Focus? Forget about it. I read a page of a book and my eyes glaze over. I'm just... numb. And sleep? Forget about it. I wake up at 3 am and just lie there staring at the ceiling. And food? I just eat because I have to. It doesn't taste like anything.

That sounds incredibly frustrating – feeling numb and struggling to concentrate, and then having sleep and appetite disrupted on top of it. It takes a lot to keep going when everything feels like a struggle. You mentioned feeling like you’re just going through the motions… have you been finding it harder to make decisions lately, even small ones?
Yeah. Everything feels like too much. I look at a menu and I just stare at it. What do I want? I don't know. It feels like I'm just watching myself do things, but I'm not really in control.

That feeling of being disconnected, like watching yourself from the outside, sounds really unsettling. It takes a lot of energy just to navigate daily life when things feel that way. When you reflect on things, do you find yourself being particularly self-critical, or holding yourself to really high standards?
Constantly. I'm my own worst enemy. I tell myself I’m just lazy or that I’m not good enough. It’s like I’m trying to punish myself for not being better.

That sounds incredibly painful – constantly being self-critical and feeling like you’re punishing yourself. It takes a lot of courage to even acknowledge that inner voice. Sometimes when we're feeling that way, emotions can feel really intense. Have you noticed yourself feeling more easily agitated or frustrated lately, or perhaps even finding yourself crying more often?
Yeah. I cry a lot. I don't know why. I just look at the ceiling and it comes out. It's embarrassing, but I feel like I'm just... empty inside, so the tears come.

That sounds incredibly overwhelming – feeling those tears come up when you’re already feeling so empty. It’s definitely not embarrassing to feel your emotions, and it takes strength to allow yourself to cry. You mentioned feeling agitated and crying more often… has that agitation shown up in other ways, like feeling more easily irritated or on edge with people?
Yeah. I snap at my friends. I say things I don't mean. I'm just so tired of being the same person every day, so I lash out. It's not fair to them, but I don't know how to stop it.

That sounds really difficult – realizing you’re lashing out at friends and feeling stuck in the same patterns. It takes a lot of self-awareness to recognize that, and it’s understandable to feel frustrated with yourself. Thinking about connecting with others, have you noticed a loss of interest in spending time with people you usually enjoy being around?
Yeah. I don't have the energy. I'd rather just stay home and stare at the wall. It feels like I'm just pretending to be a person, but I'm actually just a robot.

That feeling of being a robot, just going through the motions… that sounds incredibly isolating. It takes a lot to keep up appearances when you’re feeling that disconnected. You’ve mentioned being really hard on yourself – do you find yourself often feeling guilty about things, even small things, or holding yourself responsible for things that aren’t really your fault?
Constantly. I beat myself up over stupid stuff. I'll think, 'I should have said this,' or 'I shouldn't have done that.' It's like I'm trying to punish myself for existing.

That sounds incredibly exhausting – constantly replaying things and feeling guilty, like you’re punishing yourself just for being you. It takes a lot of strength to carry that weight. You’ve shared a lot about feeling low on energy, struggling with sleep and appetite, and being really self-critical. I’m wondering, beyond all of that, have you been feeling particularly sad or down lately, just a general sense of sadness?
Yeah. It's just... it feels like I've lost the spark. I used to be the guy who made people laugh, and now I just sit there and stare at the wall. I don't know how to get it back.

That feeling of losing your spark and not knowing how to get it back sounds incredibly disheartening. It takes a lot to be the life of the party, and it’s understandable to feel lost when that feels gone. You’ve mentioned feeling a lot of guilt and self-criticism – do you ever feel like you’re just not good enough, or that you’re a burden to others?
All the time. I think I'm just broken. I look at my friends and they're all moving forward, and I'm just stuck in this rut. I feel like I'm holding them back just by being around.

That feeling of being stuck while others move forward sounds incredibly isolating and painful. It takes a lot of courage to admit feeling like a burden, and I want you to know it’s okay to feel that way sometimes. We’ve covered a lot today, and I truly appreciate you sharing so openly with me. I think we’ve explored things in a really thorough way, and I want to thank you again for your time and honesty.
